reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) mentions spark plasma sintering as a fabrication method and general irradiation tolerance of HEAs, but provides no specific data on W38Ta36Cr15V11, no evidence that mechanical alloying suppresses Cr–V precipitates, and no support for the claimed mechanism linking homogeneity to precipitate suppression in this alloy. The key premises rely on general statements rather than direct prior results.
premises: Mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering can produce homogeneous nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloys
Enhanced chemical homogeneity reduces local Cr and V concentration fluctuations
Reduced concentration fluctuations decrease nucleation sites for Cr–V-rich precipitates under irradiation
A refined nanocrystalline matrix with high defect sink density preserves low irradiation hardening
The processing route is compatible with practical bulk manufacturability
